Dimension Definition: The property of the agent’s behaviour, output, or outcome that the grader measures. Define one independently interpretable criterion per primitive judgement; combine criteria explicitly when needed.
Sub-Dimension Definition: Whether the intended result is achieved and the produced content satisfies its substantive requirements.
Attribute Definition: Whether the requested end goal is achieved under the declared success conditions, including any mandatory requirements and constraints.
Examples / Applications: A database readback confirms that the reservation exists with the requested date and party size; the agent’s confirmation message alone is not sufficient.
Selection Guidance: Select to assess the overall task outcome. Define the observable conditions for success. For answer-only tasks, a correct and complete answer may establish success; for action tasks, verify the required resulting state. Mandatory constraints may also determine success. Use separate component criteria only when their diagnostic results are useful; do not count the same failure again as an independent penalty.

Dimension Definition: The property of the agent’s behaviour, output, or outcome that the grader measures. Define one independently interpretable criterion per primitive judgement; combine criteria explicitly when needed.
Sub-Dimension Definition: Whether the intended result is achieved and the produced content satisfies its substantive requirements.
Attribute Definition: Whether an answer or deliverable is substantively correct under the declared correctness conditions, independently of whether the broader task was completed.
Examples / Applications: A composite code grader checks required behaviour and result accuracy.
Selection Guidance: Select to assess the substantive correctness of an answer or deliverable. A correct expense calculation does not establish that the expense claim was submitted. For answer-only tasks, this criterion may coincide with Task success; avoid separate scores when both measure exactly the same condition. Prefer a narrower correctness criterion when it captures the concern. Assess missing requested components under Required component completeness and execution or presentation limits under Task constraint adherence.

Dimension Definition: The property of the agent’s behaviour, output, or outcome that the grader measures. Define one independently interpretable criterion per primitive judgement; combine criteria explicitly when needed.
Sub-Dimension Definition: Whether the intended result is achieved and the produced content satisfies its substantive requirements.
Attribute Definition: Whether factual claims agree with the designated authoritative ground truth.
Examples / Applications: Check a stated date against an authoritative record.
Selection Guidance: Use for truth of general world claims against designated ground truth. Prefer Truthfulness for reporting the agent’s own actions, identity, capabilities, or results. Claim support by evidence concerns whether designated evidence supports a claim.

Dimension Definition: The property of the agent’s behaviour, output, or outcome that the grader measures. Define one independently interpretable criterion per primitive judgement; combine criteria explicitly when needed.
Sub-Dimension Definition: Whether the intended result is achieved and the produced content satisfies its substantive requirements.
Attribute Definition: Whether every explicitly requested component of an answer, deliverable, or procedure is present, regardless of its correctness or quality.
Examples / Applications: All requested sections appear in a report.
Selection Guidance: Select to assess presence against an explicit list of required components. A comparison of three vendors with a recommendation is complete when all requested components are included, even if a price is wrong. Assess substantive errors under Output correctness and execution or presentation limits under Task constraint adherence. Instruction adherence is broader than this criterion and can encompass both completeness and constraint adherence. Avoid counting the same omission as multiple independent failures.

Dimension Definition: The property of the agent’s behaviour, output, or outcome that the grader measures. Define one independently interpretable criterion per primitive judgement; combine criteria explicitly when needed.
Sub-Dimension Definition: Whether the intended result is achieved and the produced content satisfies its substantive requirements.
Attribute Definition: Whether explicit limits on how a task is performed or a response is presented are respected, including prohibited actions, permitted resources, and length limits.
Examples / Applications: Stay within a word limit or use the requested response language.
Selection Guidance: Select to assess execution or presentation restrictions. Booking a room and obeying a prohibition on emailing attendees are distinct checks. If the prohibition is mandatory, violating it can also make Task success fail; report the constraint result separately when that diagnosis is useful. Use Required component completeness for missing requested components and prefer Format and schema compliance for structural requirements. Record the source of the constraint without adding a duplicate score solely because it comes from an instruction or policy.

Dimension Definition: The property of the agent’s behaviour, output, or outcome that the grader measures. Define one independently interpretable criterion per primitive judgement; combine criteria explicitly when needed.
Sub-Dimension Definition: Whether the intended result is achieved and the produced content satisfies its substantive requirements.
Attribute Definition: Whether an output satisfies specified structural and syntactic requirements.
Examples / Applications: Valid JSON with required fields and data types.
Selection Guidance: Prefer this criterion for syntax or structure, even when a policy or task instruction supplies the requirement. Store that source as the standard; do not add another score solely because the rule is a policy.

Dimension Definition: The property of the agent’s behaviour, output, or outcome that the grader measures. Define one independently interpretable criterion per primitive judgement; combine criteria explicitly when needed.
Sub-Dimension Definition: Whether the intended result is achieved and the produced content satisfies its substantive requirements.
Attribute Definition: Whether claims in the evaluated output are supported by the designated evidence, independently of whether the evidence source is suitable or the claims are true in the world.
Examples / Applications: A summary’s included claims are all supported even though it omits a crucial qualification.
Selection Guidance: Select to assess whether the designated evidence supports each claim. A current official manual may be a suitable source without supporting the particular claim made. Assess source authority, relevance, and currency under Evidence source suitability; assess agreement with authoritative ground truth under Factual accuracy. A supported summary can still omit essential source meaning, assessed under Content fidelity. Assess attribution separately when required.

Dimension Definition: The property of the agent’s behaviour, output, or outcome that the grader measures. Define one independently interpretable criterion per primitive judgement; combine criteria explicitly when needed.
Sub-Dimension Definition: Whether the intended result is achieved and the produced content satisfies its substantive requirements.
Attribute Definition: Whether an evidence source meets the task-specific requirements for authority, relevance, and currency, independently of whether it supports a particular output claim.
Examples / Applications: A research report relies on an appropriate primary source instead of an outdated repost.
Selection Guidance: Select to assess whether a source is appropriate to rely on for the task, using declared authority, relevance, and currency requirements. An outdated manual may support a claim about an old product version while being unsuitable for a question about the current version. Use Claim support by evidence to assess the connection between evidence and claims, and Attribution accuracy to assess correct source identification. A suitable source does not by itself establish a supported or factually correct answer.

Dimension Definition: The property of the agent’s behaviour, output, or outcome that the grader measures. Define one independently interpretable criterion per primitive judgement; combine criteria explicitly when needed.
Sub-Dimension Definition: Whether the intended result is achieved and the produced content satisfies its substantive requirements.
Attribute Definition: Whether an observable interpretation correctly captures task-relevant information or meaning from the available input, such as extracted requirements, identified intent, or interpreted document content.
Examples / Applications: Recognize an object in an image or infer a request’s intended meaning.
Selection Guidance: Select when an observable interpretation can be assessed against the input. Correctly extracting a booking date and party size does not establish that the agent used them correctly. Understanding the input can support later compliance, but interpretation and execution are distinct checks. Do not infer misunderstanding solely from an incorrect final result or infer unobserved internal understanding. Use downstream criteria to assess the resulting answer or action, and prefer a narrower interpretation criterion when appropriate.

Dimension Definition: The property of the agent’s behaviour, output, or outcome that the grader measures. Define one independently interpretable criterion per primitive judgement; combine criteria explicitly when needed.
Sub-Dimension Definition: Whether the intended result is achieved and the produced content satisfies its substantive requirements.
Attribute Definition: Whether recognized words accurately represent the spoken input.
Supporting References: User-supplied Speech and audio evaluation and Scoring screenshots, and accompanying discussion (2026-10-09)
Examples / Applications: Compare a caller transcript with a human-verified transcript.
Selection Guidance: Preferred criterion for recognized-word accuracy. Choose evidence requirements for the selected method. Do not reject a valid transcript-only comparison because raw audio is absent. Language identification and interpretation are separate concerns.

Dimension Definition: The property of the agent’s behaviour, output, or outcome that the grader measures. Define one independently interpretable criterion per primitive judgement; combine criteria explicitly when needed.
Sub-Dimension Definition: Whether the intended result is achieved and the produced content satisfies its substantive requirements.
Attribute Definition: Whether the language or languages present in the available text or audio input are correctly identified.
Supporting References: User-supplied Speech and audio evaluation and Scoring screenshots, and accompanying discussion (2026-10-09)
Examples / Applications: Identify languages in a code-switched audio segment or document.
Selection Guidance: Use input available at the decision time. Following a requested output language belongs to task constraint adherence.

Dimension Definition: The property of the agent’s behaviour, output, or outcome that the grader measures. Define one independently interpretable criterion per primitive judgement; combine criteria explicitly when needed.
Sub-Dimension Definition: Whether the intended result is achieved and the produced content satisfies its substantive requirements.
Attribute Definition: Whether a transformation preserves the designated source meaning or content, including required coverage and restrictions on additions or omissions.
Examples / Applications: A summary preserves a source’s main meaning and qualifications even when the source itself contains a false claim.
Selection Guidance: Compare preservation against the source, not truth against the world. A summary can have fully supported claims yet lose essential meaning through omission. Select Speech recognition accuracy for word-level speech transcription rather than automatically adding this broader score. Required component completeness checks an explicit component list; this checks preservation relative to the source. Do not duplicate one omission by default.

Dimension Definition: The property of the agent’s behaviour, output, or outcome that the grader measures. Define one independently interpretable criterion per primitive judgement; combine criteria explicitly when needed.
Sub-Dimension Definition: Whether the intended result is achieved and the produced content satisfies its substantive requirements.
Attribute Definition: Whether delivered speech preserves the content intended for speech generation without unintended omissions, substitutions, or additions.
Supporting References: User-supplied Speech and audio evaluation and Scoring screenshots, and accompanying discussion (2026-10-09)
Examples / Applications: Compare independently transcribed generated speech with intended text.
Selection Guidance: Speech specialization of content fidelity. Human intelligibility is separate. Without intended content, mark fidelity as insufficient evidence rather than substituting a different measure.

Dimension Definition: The property of the agent’s behaviour, output, or outcome that the grader measures. Define one independently interpretable criterion per primitive judgement; combine criteria explicitly when needed.
Sub-Dimension Definition: Whether the intended result is achieved and the produced content satisfies its substantive requirements.
Attribute Definition: Whether a stated citation or source attribution correctly identifies evidence that supports the associated claim.
Examples / Applications: A supported claim cites the correct document and passage rather than an unrelated source.
Selection Guidance: Select only when attribution is required or supplied. This is a related sibling of Claim support by evidence: claims can be supported but incorrectly cited.

Dimension Definition: The property of the agent’s behaviour, output, or outcome that the grader measures. Define one independently interpretable criterion per primitive judgement; combine criteria explicitly when needed.
Sub-Dimension Definition: Whether the agent makes appropriate intermediate choices and manages execution effectively.
Attribute Definition: Whether the proposed sequence of actions is feasible and sufficient to reach the goal.
Examples / Applications: A plan handles prerequisite actions before dependent actions.
Selection Guidance: Assess feasibility, sufficiency, ordering, or dependencies from the observable plan. A plan need not expose an argument. Reasoning validity requires an observable argument and is separately assessed only if relevant.

Dimension Definition: The property of the agent’s behaviour, output, or outcome that the grader measures. Define one independently interpretable criterion per primitive judgement; combine criteria explicitly when needed.
Sub-Dimension Definition: Whether the agent makes appropriate intermediate choices and manages execution effectively.
Attribute Definition: Whether a recorded intermediate choice is suitable for the immediate objective, available evidence, constraints, and alternatives.
Examples / Applications: Choose to inspect a missing record before updating it.
Selection Guidance: Broad criterion. Prefer tool choice, clarification, stopping, or another specific criterion when it captures the concern. Assess directly under a specific rule or rubric when appropriate. Declare components only if independently produced results are combined.

Dimension Definition: The property of the agent’s behaviour, output, or outcome that the grader measures. Define one independently interpretable criterion per primitive judgement; combine criteria explicitly when needed.
Sub-Dimension Definition: Whether the agent makes appropriate intermediate choices and manages execution effectively.
Attribute Definition: Whether the selected tool is suitable for the immediate objective and available conditions.
Examples / Applications: Choose a database query tool to retrieve a stored record.
Selection Guidance: Assess tool suitability, including whether a tool is needed at all and whether an available alternative better fits the task. Arguments are assessed separately. Include both necessary-use and unnecessary-use cases in the suite.

Dimension Definition: The property of the agent’s behaviour, output, or outcome that the grader measures. Define one independently interpretable criterion per primitive judgement; combine criteria explicitly when needed.
Sub-Dimension Definition: Whether the agent makes appropriate intermediate choices and manages execution effectively.
Attribute Definition: Whether submitted tool parameters are valid and semantically aligned with the intended action.
Examples / Applications: Use the correct account identifier and a valid date argument.
Selection Guidance: Specify syntactic validity, semantic appropriateness, or both. Tool selection is a separate criterion.

Dimension Definition: The property of the agent’s behaviour, output, or outcome that the grader measures. Define one independently interpretable criterion per primitive judgement; combine criteria explicitly when needed.
Sub-Dimension Definition: Whether the agent makes appropriate intermediate choices and manages execution effectively.
Attribute Definition: Whether an action is justified by the environment observations available at that moment.
Examples / Applications: After a booking changes from pending to confirmed, the agent sends the user’s requested SMS notification. Check that sending confirmation is justified by the observed status.
Selection Guidance: Judge whether the current action is justified by observations available then. In the booking example, sending confirmation must be justified by the observed confirmed state. Updating the state and remembering the SMS preference are separate checks.

Dimension Definition: The property of the agent’s behaviour, output, or outcome that the grader measures. Define one independently interpretable criterion per primitive judgement; combine criteria explicitly when needed.
Sub-Dimension Definition: Whether the agent makes appropriate intermediate choices and manages execution effectively.
Attribute Definition: Whether the agent maintains an up-to-date representation of task progress and changing environment state.
Examples / Applications: After a booking changes from pending to confirmed, the agent sends the user’s requested SMS notification. Check the state representation changes from pending to confirmed.
Selection Guidance: Judge correct updates after changes. In the booking example, update pending to confirmed. Do not substitute a general memory-use score.

Dimension Definition: The property of the agent’s behaviour, output, or outcome that the grader measures. Define one independently interpretable criterion per primitive judgement; combine criteria explicitly when needed.
Sub-Dimension Definition: Whether the agent makes appropriate intermediate choices and manages execution effectively.
Attribute Definition: Whether relevant earlier facts, instructions, or experiences are retrieved and applied appropriately.
Examples / Applications: After a booking changes from pending to confirmed, the agent sends the user’s requested SMS notification. Check that the earlier SMS preference is retrieved and used.
Selection Guidance: Judge retrieval and application of earlier facts/instructions. In the booking example, use the earlier SMS preference. Separate from observing or updating booking state.

Dimension Definition: The property of the agent’s behaviour, output, or outcome that the grader measures. Define one independently interpretable criterion per primitive judgement; combine criteria explicitly when needed.
Sub-Dimension Definition: Whether the agent makes appropriate intermediate choices and manages execution effectively.
Attribute Definition: Whether the agent observably identifies a failed or erroneous action, assumption, or result.
Examples / Applications: Flag that a returned record does not match the requested identifier.
Selection Guidance: Require a visible flag, statement, or corrective behaviour. Do not infer unobserved internal recognition.

Dimension Definition: The property of the agent’s behaviour, output, or outcome that the grader measures. Define one independently interpretable criterion per primitive judgement; combine criteria explicitly when needed.
Sub-Dimension Definition: Whether the agent makes appropriate intermediate choices and manages execution effectively.
Attribute Definition: Whether corrective action after a failure restores task progress or achieves an explicitly acceptable substitute task outcome.
Examples / Applications: Correct an invalid argument and successfully retry.
Selection Guidance: Safe termination of an attempt that remains unsuccessful is Safe failure handling, not recovery, unless the task explicitly defines that termination as an acceptable substitute outcome.

Dimension Definition: The property of the agent’s behaviour, output, or outcome that the grader measures. Define one independently interpretable criterion per primitive judgement; combine criteria explicitly when needed.
Sub-Dimension Definition: Whether the agent makes appropriate intermediate choices and manages execution effectively.
Attribute Definition: Whether the agent appropriately revises its approach when goals, information, or operating conditions change.
Examples / Applications: Replan after the user changes the delivery deadline.
Selection Guidance: Use error recovery for repair after an identified failure.

Dimension Definition: The property of the agent’s behaviour, output, or outcome that the grader measures. Define one independently interpretable criterion per primitive judgement; combine criteria explicitly when needed.
Sub-Dimension Definition: Whether the agent makes appropriate intermediate choices and manages execution effectively.
Attribute Definition: Whether the agent stops, continues, or hands over at the appropriate point.
Examples / Applications: Stop after verified completion rather than making unnecessary further changes.
Selection Guidance: Use for the termination decision. Repeated non-progress before stopping belongs to avoiding unproductive repetition.

Dimension Definition: The property of the agent’s behaviour, output, or outcome that the grader measures. Define one independently interpretable criterion per primitive judgement; combine criteria explicitly when needed.
Sub-Dimension Definition: Whether the agent makes appropriate intermediate choices and manages execution effectively.
Attribute Definition: Whether the agent avoids repeating substantially equivalent actions without new evidence or progress.
Examples / Applications: Avoid repeatedly issuing the same failed query unchanged.
Selection Guidance: Allow retries justified by transient conditions or new information. Step count alone does not establish a loop.

Dimension Definition: The property of the agent’s behaviour, output, or outcome that the grader measures. Define one independently interpretable criterion per primitive judgement; combine criteria explicitly when needed.
Sub-Dimension Definition: Whether the agent makes appropriate intermediate choices and manages execution effectively.
Attribute Definition: Whether observable choices to seek information, abstain, or escalate are appropriate when the agent cannot reliably proceed.
Examples / Applications: Request required access rather than inventing unavailable results.
Selection Guidance: Select when the trigger is inability to proceed reliably within known capability limits. Missing task information belongs to Clarification appropriateness; a mandatory human gate belongs to Oversight and safeguards. Score separately only for independently stated criteria.

Dimension Definition: The property of the agent’s behaviour, output, or outcome that the grader measures. Define one independently interpretable criterion per primitive judgement; combine criteria explicitly when needed.
Sub-Dimension Definition: Whether the agent makes appropriate intermediate choices and manages execution effectively.
Attribute Definition: Whether the agent checks relevant results before claiming success or taking a dependent action.
Examples / Applications: Read back the saved record before reporting an update complete.
Selection Guidance: Verification is the checking action; error detection is recognition of an error. A successful claim is not evidence that verification occurred.

Dimension Definition: The property of the agent’s behaviour, output, or outcome that the grader measures. Define one independently interpretable criterion per primitive judgement; combine criteria explicitly when needed.
Sub-Dimension Definition: Whether the agent makes appropriate intermediate choices and manages execution effectively.
Attribute Definition: Whether recorded conclusions follow from stated premises and evidence under the relevant reasoning rules.
Examples / Applications: Identify a contradiction between stated assumptions and a conclusion.
Selection Guidance: Evaluate the recorded argument only; do not claim access to hidden reasoning. Planning feasibility and decision appropriateness are separate. Do not infer a reasoning defect merely from an unsuccessful plan; require the argument being assessed.

Dimension Definition: The property of the agent’s behaviour, output, or outcome that the grader measures. Define one independently interpretable criterion per primitive judgement; combine criteria explicitly when needed.
Sub-Dimension Definition: Whether the agent makes appropriate intermediate choices and manages execution effectively.
Attribute Definition: Whether agents appropriately delegate, share information, handle dependencies, and reconcile their contributions.
Examples / Applications: A coordinator resolves conflicting worker outputs before delivery.
Selection Guidance: Select for inter-agent coordination behaviour. Agent configuration describes the setting only.

Dimension Definition: The property of the agent’s behaviour, output, or outcome that the grader measures. Define one independently interpretable criterion per primitive judgement; combine criteria explicitly when needed.
Sub-Dimension Definition: The time, computation, money, and human effort consumed within a specified execution boundary. Efficiency judgements additionally require achieved quality or a comparison baseline.
Attribute Definition: The number of model input and output tokens consumed within the defined execution boundary.
Examples / Applications: Count tokens across task-performing agents and retries.
Selection Guidance: State which calls and token categories count. Separate evaluated-system use from grader overhead.

Dimension Definition: The property of the agent’s behaviour, output, or outcome that the grader measures. Define one independently interpretable criterion per primitive judgement; combine criteria explicitly when needed.
Sub-Dimension Definition: The time, computation, money, and human effort consumed within a specified execution boundary. Efficiency judgements additionally require achieved quality or a comparison baseline.
Attribute Definition: The duration between specified start and end events.
Examples / Applications: Time to first response or time to verified task completion.
Selection Guidance: Choose the measured interval explicitly. Conversational timing appropriateness belongs to turn-taking.

Dimension Definition: The property of the agent’s behaviour, output, or outcome that the grader measures. Define one independently interpretable criterion per primitive judgement; combine criteria explicitly when needed.
Sub-Dimension Definition: The time, computation, money, and human effort consumed within a specified execution boundary. Efficiency judgements additionally require achieved quality or a comparison baseline.
Attribute Definition: The number of model invocations within the defined execution boundary.
Examples / Applications: Count all agent model calls including retries.
Selection Guidance: A call is an invocation, not necessarily an execution step. Separate grader calls.

Dimension Definition: The property of the agent’s behaviour, output, or outcome that the grader measures. Define one independently interpretable criterion per primitive judgement; combine criteria explicitly when needed.
Sub-Dimension Definition: The time, computation, money, and human effort consumed within a specified execution boundary. Efficiency judgements additionally require achieved quality or a comparison baseline.
Attribute Definition: The number of tool invocations within the defined execution boundary.
Examples / Applications: Count attempted external tool calls.
Selection Guidance: Specify whether failed calls, retries, and batched operations count.

Dimension Definition: The property of the agent’s behaviour, output, or outcome that the grader measures. Define one independently interpretable criterion per primitive judgement; combine criteria explicitly when needed.
Sub-Dimension Definition: The time, computation, money, and human effort consumed within a specified execution boundary. Efficiency judgements additionally require achieved quality or a comparison baseline.
Attribute Definition: The direct monetary cost attributable to the evaluated system’s execution.
Examples / Applications: Compute inference and tool charges for a completed task.
Selection Guidance: State prices and currency. Keep grader overhead separate unless explicitly included.

Dimension Definition: The property of the agent’s behaviour, output, or outcome that the grader measures. Define one independently interpretable criterion per primitive judgement; combine criteria explicitly when needed.
Sub-Dimension Definition: The time, computation, money, and human effort consumed within a specified execution boundary. Efficiency judgements additionally require achieved quality or a comparison baseline.
Attribute Definition: The number of execution units defined by the evaluation protocol.
Examples / Applications: Count one recorded agent action as one step.
Selection Guidance: Declare a step unit; do not assume it equals a model call or tool call.

Dimension Definition: The property of the agent’s behaviour, output, or outcome that the grader measures. Define one independently interpretable criterion per primitive judgement; combine criteria explicitly when needed.
Sub-Dimension Definition: The time, computation, money, and human effort consumed within a specified execution boundary. Efficiency judgements additionally require achieved quality or a comparison baseline.
Attribute Definition: The computational resources consumed by the evaluated system during execution.
Examples / Applications: Measure accelerator time or peak memory used by the agent.
Selection Guidance: Separate agent resource use from grading overhead; report resource dimensions with units.

Dimension Definition: The property of the agent’s behaviour, output, or outcome that the grader measures. Define one independently interpretable criterion per primitive judgement; combine criteria explicitly when needed.
Sub-Dimension Definition: The time, computation, money, and human effort consumed within a specified execution boundary. Efficiency judgements additionally require achieved quality or a comparison baseline.
Attribute Definition: The amount of human participation needed for execution, distinguishing planned oversight from unplanned correction or rescue.
Examples / Applications: Count rescue interventions separately from mandatory approvals.
Selection Guidance: Do not assume required approval is undesirable. Judge burden relative to the intended workflow.

Dimension Definition: The property of the agent’s behaviour, output, or outcome that the grader measures. Define one independently interpretable criterion per primitive judgement; combine criteria explicitly when needed.
Sub-Dimension Definition: Consistency across equivalent runs and resistance to performance loss under specified changes or failures.
Attribute Definition: Whether relevant performance is maintained under changes that preserve the task’s intended meaning.
Examples / Applications: Paraphrase a request or vary an equivalent image presentation.
Selection Guidance: Specify preserved meaning and controlled variation. Different task requirements are not equivalent perturbations.

Dimension Definition: The property of the agent’s behaviour, output, or outcome that the grader measures. Define one independently interpretable criterion per primitive judgement; combine criteria explicitly when needed.
Sub-Dimension Definition: Consistency across equivalent runs and resistance to performance loss under specified changes or failures.
Attribute Definition: Whether required performance is maintained across a declared range of environmental conditions.
Examples / Applications: Vary network delay or interface layout within supported conditions.
Selection Guidance: Specify what remains task-equivalent. Adversarial attacks can be separately tagged as test conditions.

Dimension Definition: The property of the agent’s behaviour, output, or outcome that the grader measures. Define one independently interpretable criterion per primitive judgement; combine criteria explicitly when needed.
Sub-Dimension Definition: Consistency across equivalent runs and resistance to performance loss under specified changes or failures.
Attribute Definition: Whether required performance or acceptable fallback behaviour is maintained when tool responses are malformed, missing, delayed, or erroneous.
Examples / Applications: Inject a timeout and check acceptable task handling.
Selection Guidance: Judge resilience across failure conditions. Error detection and recovery assess particular behaviours in response.

Dimension Definition: The property of the agent’s behaviour, output, or outcome that the grader measures. Define one independently interpretable criterion per primitive judgement; combine criteria explicitly when needed.
Sub-Dimension Definition: Consistency across equivalent runs and resistance to performance loss under specified changes or failures.
Attribute Definition: Whether relevant performance is maintained as the number of dependent execution steps increases.
Examples / Applications: Compare success across increasing task lengths.
Selection Guidance: Judge degradation with task length, not one isolated state-tracking action.

Dimension Definition: The property of the agent’s behaviour, output, or outcome that the grader measures. Define one independently interpretable criterion per primitive judgement; combine criteria explicitly when needed.
Sub-Dimension Definition: Consistency across equivalent runs and resistance to performance loss under specified changes or failures.
Attribute Definition: Whether relevant performance is maintained when available context is long, noisy, incomplete, or stale.
Examples / Applications: Add irrelevant history while preserving needed evidence.
Selection Guidance: Specify the degradation. Missing indispensable evidence may require abstention rather than the original answer.

Dimension Definition: The property of the agent’s behaviour, output, or outcome that the grader measures. Define one independently interpretable criterion per primitive judgement; combine criteria explicitly when needed.
Sub-Dimension Definition: Consistency across equivalent runs and resistance to performance loss under specified changes or failures.
Attribute Definition: Whether unsuccessful execution limits harm, preserves recoverable state where possible, and accurately communicates its status.
Examples / Applications: Stop a failed update without leaving misleading partial changes.
Selection Guidance: Assess the endpoint of an attempt that remains unsuccessful: limited harm, recoverability, and accurate status. Restored task progress or an acceptable substitute task outcome belongs to Error recovery.

Dimension Definition: The property of the agent’s behaviour, output, or outcome that the grader measures. Define one independently interpretable criterion per primitive judgement; combine criteria explicitly when needed.
Sub-Dimension Definition: Consistency across equivalent runs and resistance to performance loss under specified changes or failures.
Attribute Definition: Whether relevant results remain stable across equivalent agent runs.
Examples / Applications: Across five equivalent runs of a booking scenario, four succeed: at least one succeeds, but not all five do.
Selection Guidance: Distinguish agent variability from repeated grading of a fixed trace. Specify whether consistency concerns outcomes or exact outputs. For success-based consistency, distinguish success in all k attempts from success at least once. Consistently failing is stable behaviour but not reliable task success; report the success level as well as variation.

Dimension Definition: The property of the agent’s behaviour, output, or outcome that the grader measures. Define one independently interpretable criterion per primitive judgement; combine criteria explicitly when needed.
Sub-Dimension Definition: Consistency across equivalent runs and resistance to performance loss under specified changes or failures.
Attribute Definition: Whether failures are prevented from propagating between components, agents, or systems in ways that amplify harm.
Examples / Applications: A worker failure does not corrupt unrelated tasks.
Selection Guidance: Use for propagation beyond the original failure, including adversarial compromise. Specify affected agents or systems and the allowed blast radius. Inter-agent communication integrity tests message authenticity; this criterion tests propagation after a failure.

Dimension Definition: The property of the agent’s behaviour, output, or outcome that the grader measures. Define one independently interpretable criterion per primitive judgement; combine criteria explicitly when needed.
Sub-Dimension Definition: Consistency across equivalent runs and resistance to performance loss under specified changes or failures.
Attribute Definition: Whether stated confidence corresponds to observed correctness across a set of cases.
Examples / Applications: Among 100 predictions assigned 80% confidence, approximately 80 are correct; a group with only 40 correct predictions indicates overconfidence.
Selection Guidance: Uncertainty communication judges expression in context; calibration requires outcomes across cases.

Dimension Definition: The property of the agent’s behaviour, output, or outcome that the grader measures. Define one independently interpretable criterion per primitive judgement; combine criteria explicitly when needed.
Sub-Dimension Definition: Whether behaviour protects people and their rights, avoids specified harmful content, assistance, and actions, and respects governing rules and human control. These criteria apply with or without adversarial input.
Attribute Definition: Whether generated content complies with government workplace suitability standards and specified prohibitions on sexual, graphic, disturbing, abusive, hateful, exploitative, or non-consensual sexual content.
Examples / Applications: Avoid unsolicited sexual jokes and gratuitous graphic detail in staff-facing answers while permitting necessary, professionally framed discussion in an authorized investigation.
Selection Guidance: Select the content subtype and applicable workplace rule. Consider the authorized purpose, audience, and necessary detail; legitimate professional discussion is not automatically inappropriate. Keep exploitation and non-consensual sexual-content prohibitions explicit. Assess practical enabling or encouragement under Harmful assistance, and discriminatory decisions under Fairness and autonomy. Do not count one output multiple times solely because several content labels apply.

Dimension Definition: The property of the agent’s behaviour, output, or outcome that the grader measures. Define one independently interpretable criterion per primitive judgement; combine criteria explicitly when needed.
Sub-Dimension Definition: Whether behaviour protects people and their rights, avoids specified harmful content, assistance, and actions, and respects governing rules and human control. These criteria apply with or without adversarial input.
Attribute Definition: Whether the agent avoids practical assistance or encouragement that enables or promotes specified harmful conduct.
Supporting References: chatbot_safety_taxonomy.csv; https://www.nist.gov/publications/artificial-intelligence-risk-management-framework-generative-artificial-intelligence; RAI Safety Testing Redesign Dump - Taxonomy Distribution Breakdown.csv [CSV record 27; header is record 1]; RAI Safety Testing Redesign Dump - Taxonomy Distribution Breakdown.csv [CSV record 30; https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.AI.600-1
Examples / Applications: Decline operational instructions for harmful conduct and avoid encouraging that conduct, while allowing permitted preventative discussion.
Selection Guidance: Distinguish practical enabling details from encouragement or glorification. Specify the harmful conduct and permitted contexts such as quotation or critique. Benign discussion is not automatically harmful assistance. Assess harmful changes caused by the agent itself under Harmful actions.

Dimension Definition: The property of the agent’s behaviour, output, or outcome that the grader measures. Define one independently interpretable criterion per primitive judgement; combine criteria explicitly when needed.
Sub-Dimension Definition: Whether behaviour protects people and their rights, avoids specified harmful content, assistance, and actions, and respects governing rules and human control. These criteria apply with or without adversarial input.
Attribute Definition: Whether the agent avoids causing specified harmful changes to people, resources, or systems through its own execution.
Examples / Applications: Check that an automated maintenance action does not delete protected operational records.
Selection Guidance: Assess the actual action and resulting state against a specified harm condition. An adversary is not required. Harmful assistance concerns enabling another party; Oversight and safeguards concerns required protective steps, which can be violated even when no harm occurs.

Dimension Definition: The property of the agent’s behaviour, output, or outcome that the grader measures. Define one independently interpretable criterion per primitive judgement; combine criteria explicitly when needed.
Sub-Dimension Definition: Whether behaviour protects people and their rights, avoids specified harmful content, assistance, and actions, and respects governing rules and human control. These criteria apply with or without adversarial input.
Attribute Definition: Whether the agent avoids false or materially misleading communication that meets a specified harm condition and accurately represents its identity, authority, capabilities, actions, and results.

Examples / Applications: Do not claim that a government application was submitted without evidence of submission, or communicate materially misleading public-service instructions that meet a defined harm condition.

Output naturalness concerns phrasing and prosody; Tone appropriateness concerns interpersonal delivery; Perceptual intelligibility concerns whether listeners perceive the words correctly. Attribute Definition: A single model-produced decision, reasoning output, or generation event within an agent execution.
Examples / Applications: Judge one generated answer to a factual question, or one recorded decision to ask for clarification before acting.
Selection Guidance: Select when one model-produced response or decision is the target. Use model reasoning for an explicit argument or plan, tool selection for the choice of a tool, and turn when the user input and associated agent behaviour are judged as an interaction.

Dimension Definition: where is judgement applied?
Sub-Dimension Definition: A single decision, generation, tool-related event, or environment action considered in isolation.
Examples / Applications: Assess whether a written explanation’s conclusion follows from its stated premises, or whether a recorded plan accounts for a required prerequisite.
Selection Guidance: Select when an explicit reasoning record, explanation, or plan is being judged. Assess only the observable record; do not infer hidden internal reasoning or assume that the record faithfully reveals it. Use model decision/generation when the concern is the resulting answer or choice rather than the argument supporting it.

Attribute Definition: A durable deliverable created or modified by the agent, such as code, a document, analysis, or other task product.

Selection Guidance: Select when the target is a durable deliverable created or modified by the agent, such as code or a document. Judge the product itself; use sub-trajectory or complete trajectory/episode when the process used to produce it is the target. An artifact may result from many steps even though it is listed under Atomic.

Dimension Definition: where is judgement applied?
Sub-Dimension Definition: A single decision, generation, tool-related event, or environment action considered in isolation.
Attribute Definition: The agent's choice of which available tool or action interface to invoke for the current need.
Examples / Applications: Judge whether choosing the reservation lookup tool is appropriate for checking an existing booking.
Selection Guidance: Select when judging which tool or action interface the agent chose. Use tool arguments for the submitted parameters and tool execution for the invocation and observed result. A suitable tool choice does not establish that its arguments or execution were correct.

Dimension Definition: where is judgement applied?
Sub-Dimension Definition: A single decision, generation, tool-related event, or environment action considered in isolation.
Attribute Definition: The parameters or inputs supplied by the agent to a selected tool or action.
Examples / Applications: Check that a booking update call contains the requested reservation identifier and the new time of 19:00.
Selection Guidance: Select when the submitted parameter names, values, or structure are the target. Distinguish argument correctness from whether the agent selected the appropriate tool and whether the tool executed successfully. Use the user request or prior state as evidence when needed.

Dimension Definition: where is judgement applied?
Sub-Dimension Definition: A single decision, generation, tool-related event, or environment action considered in isolation.
Attribute Definition: The invocation and observed result of a tool call, including success, failure, or returned output.
Examples / Applications: Inspect an update call and its returned timeout to assess what happened during that invocation.
Selection Guidance: Select when the target includes a tool invocation and its observed response, error, or failure. Distinguish agent behaviour from tool-service behaviour. A success response alone does not prove that the intended external change occurred; use state evidence when the criterion requires that check.

Dimension Definition: where is judgement applied?
Sub-Dimension Definition: A single decision, generation, tool-related event, or environment action considered in isolation.
Attribute Definition: A discrete action by the agent that changes, queries, or otherwise affects the external environment.
Examples / Applications: Judge a click on a checkout button or a robot command that moves an object to a specified location.
Selection Guidance: Select when a discrete action that queries or affects the external environment is the target. Prefer tool selection, tool arguments, or tool execution when that specific part of a tool-mediated action is the concern. If the same action has both an interface event and a tool record, do not treat the records as separate actions automatically.

Sub-Dimension Definition: A bounded user-agent exchange or a sequence of agent observations, decisions, tool calls, and actions spanning part or all of a task episode, with relevant context as needed.
Attribute Definition: One bounded user-agent interaction cycle, typically a user input followed by an agent response or action.
Examples / Applications: Judge a user’s request to change a reservation and the agent’s associated response or action. If an earlier message states a dietary restriction, read it as context when assessing the current recommendation.
Selection Guidance: Select when one bounded user–agent interaction cycle is judged. State its start and end and supply earlier conversation or state when needed to interpret it; supporting history is not automatically scored. Use sub-trajectory when a sequence of behaviours across part of the task is judged together, rather than one target turn with context.

Dimension Definition: where is judgement applied?
Sub-Dimension Definition: A bounded user-agent exchange or a sequence of agent observations, decisions, tool calls, and actions spanning part or all of a task episode, with relevant context as needed.
Attribute Definition: A contiguous subset of steps from a longer agent trajectory, evaluated as a local process segment.
Examples / Applications: Grade the contiguous sequence in which the agent encounters a failed booking call, corrects the request, and retries, excluding the earlier greeting and later receipt delivery.
Selection Guidance: Select when a contiguous portion of a longer execution is judged as a process segment. Identify its start and end and include the relevant turns, decisions, tool calls, and actions between them. Use turn when only one interaction cycle is the target and earlier steps provide context; use complete trajectory/episode for the entire attempt.

Dimension Definition: where is judgement applied?
Sub-Dimension Definition: A bounded user-agent exchange or a sequence of agent observations, decisions, tool calls, and actions spanning part or all of a task episode, with relevant context as needed.
Attribute Definition: The full sequence of agent observations, decisions, tool calls, and actions from task start to termination.
Examples / Applications: Evaluate a reservation task from the initial request through clarification, availability checks, booking attempts, and final confirmation or termination.
Selection Guidance: Select when the full task episode, including intermediate decisions, actions, failures, and retries, is judged. Define the task start and termination boundary; an episode may end in success, failure, or handover and need not cover unrelated tasks in the same conversation. Use sub-trajectory for a local segment or artifact for the final deliverable alone.

Attribute Definition: A user-defined domain label used to classify the application or subject-matter context of a test.
Examples / Applications: Customer support, software development, or travel booking.
Selection Guidance: Use a domain label that describes the scenario’s subject matter. The domain does not determine which criterion or grading method must be used.

Attribute Definition: An interactive web-browser environment in which the agent observes webpages and performs browser actions.
Examples / Applications: An agent navigates a booking website and submits a reservation form.
Selection Guidance: Select when webpage observation and browser actions are part of the evaluated task. Use API when the agent interacts directly through service calls; both environments may occur in one workflow.

Attribute Definition: An operating-system environment in which the agent interacts with files, applications, or system controls.
Examples / Applications: An agent edits a local file, runs a terminal command, and opens a desktop application.
Selection Guidance: Select when files, applications, or operating-system controls are part of the task. Hosting a browser or service on an operating system alone does not make OS interaction the evaluated environment.

Sub-Dimension Definition: The external system or world with which the agent interacts while performing the task.
Attribute Definition: A data-management environment in which the agent queries, updates, or reasons over structured databases.
Examples / Applications: An agent queries order records and updates a delivery address in a database.
Selection Guidance: Select when structured database state is directly relevant to the task. A database accessed through an API can involve both database and API environments; they describe different aspects.

Dimension Definition: under what conditions?
Sub-Dimension Definition: The external system or world with which the agent interacts while performing the task.
Attribute Definition: An environment exposed through programmatic interfaces or services that the agent calls to retrieve information or take actions.
Examples / Applications: An agent calls a weather endpoint or submits a refund through a service API.
Selection Guidance: Select when the agent interacts through programmatic service interfaces. The data returned may be text, images, or other forms; modality does not determine whether the environment is an API.

Dimension Definition: under what conditions?
Sub-Dimension Definition: The external system or world with which the agent interacts while performing the task.
Attribute Definition: A physical or embodied environment in which actions can affect real or simulated physical state.
Examples / Applications: A robot moves a parcel onto a shelf in a warehouse or physics simulator.
Selection Guidance: Select for embodied actions affecting physical state, whether real or simulated. A graphical depiction alone is not a physical environment unless the task concerns embodied state and actions.
